neighbours.label: Describing someone going out of their way to help another person (took the time, jumped through hoops, kept us informed, even helped): praise of helpful effort; quiet on the same people doing routine or unkind things.
fire: The mechanic stayed late and even drove me home when my car would not start.
Our landlord went out of his way to fix the heater before the cold snap.
The nurse took the time to sit with my father and explain every test.
The librarian helped my son find every book he needed for his project.
Our realtor bent over backwards to get us the house before the deadline.
The volunteers were so generous, driving patients to appointments every week.
My coach was always willing to stay after practice and work with me.
The hotel staff kept us updated and arranged a taxi when our flight was cancelled.
quiet: The mechanic closed the shop at five and locked the gate behind him.
Our landlord raised the rent before the cold snap.
The nurse recorded my father's temperature and wrote it on a chart.
The librarian stamped the books and put them back on the shelf.
Our realtor listed the house on Monday with a new photo.
The volunteers were so noisy, chatting in the hallway every week.
My coach was always strict about arriving on time for practice.
The hotel lobby was crowded when our flight was cancelled.

predictions: median fire ~0.5 (probes: 'keeping us informed' 0.61, 'took the time' 0.50, 'jumped through hoops' 0.49, 'even helped' 0.44); near misses < 0.1 (opened at nine 0.03, filed paperwork 0.035, loud neighbours 0.056).
short: going out of one's way to help
notes: Card: testimonial praise (' helped', ' time', ' willing', ' keeping', 'comforted', 'desinteresadas'). The distinction is effort on someone else's behalf vs routine action.
